Why go: Lamai Bay from 10 minutes in the air

Parasailing gives you the best view of Lamai: the whole curve of the bay, the reef line, Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks at the south end and the hills behind. Launch and landing are from the boat, so there is no running start on the sand and it suits nervous first-timers better than the old beach-launch style.

Flights are short, so this is a one-hour stop rather than a day out. It pairs well with a morning in Lamai or lunch on the beach.

Solo or tandem

A solo flight gives the longest, steadiest ride for one person. Tandem flights put two people side by side under one canopy; they cost less per person and suit couples, friends and parents flying with a child. Either way the flight lasts about 10 minutes, and the crew controls height and landing from the boat. Book for the morning if you can: the sea is usually calmer, the light is softer for photos, and the afternoon sea breeze that can stop flights hasn't built yet.

Who it suits

  • Couples, who can fly tandem.
  • Families with older children who want a quick thrill.
  • Anyone staying in Lamai or nearby Chaweng.

Who should choose something else

  • Anyone visiting from November to January, when the east coast is often too windy: consider the jungle zipline instead.
  • People who want more time on the water: our jet ski safari to Pig Island or a Pig Island speedboat tour.

Good to know

  • Weather: flights depend on wind and sea state. Calm mornings are best.
  • Safety: follow the crew's hand signals and keep straps tight. Don't fly after drinking.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time; the crew confirms your slot.
